When going rod fishing you should first throw the fishing rod into the water, and then you have a good fishing luck.
The very first fish of the spring that you catch with a fishing rod in open water season should be thrown back into the water to please the spirit of the water and assure your future fishing luck.

When first fish of the spring are caught out at a lake in open water season, make a fish soup or boil them right after returning on shore. When it's cooked, go away from the pot so that the spirit of the water can have the first taste.
You get a good catch if you step in the punt backwards and launch it in the water backwards.
making a bird thief to confess

Bird thief will come confess if you take three feathers that have remained from the stolen bird and throw them into heated sauna stove after the fire has burnt out. You can also throw the feathers into remains of burnt-out fire which was made on base rock.
making a squirrel stay still in a tree
Turn around and kick a tree with your heel and the squirrel will then stay still in there, even if it would have been jumping around a lot earlier.

Have a capercaillie feather with you when chasing a lynx. The feather is then put on lynx tracks from where it first fled, on its very first escaping tracks. This will burden the lynx, making it more quickly fatigued.
Be it birds or hares you are after, the loop snares you are about to use are made favorable by leaving them in an ant nest for three nights, and only then picked up and set for a catch.
To make a fox trap favourable leave it laying at doorstep of a building where womenfolk will get to walk over it.
making foxes to come at the bait
Baiting a fox-trap at your hunting grounds should be done just around sunset.
Loop snares for hares shouldn't be set barehanded but you should always wear mittens, and preferably woollen mittens.
carrying bear teeth to find hares and birds
Bear is a great hunter who always finds its prey, and hunters who carry bear teeth with them can come across hares and game birds as they please.
When deadfall trap is made for a bear you should then set the meat bait there completely naked. Then the bear gets in there nicely.
Bear hunter's mittens shouldn't be made of whatever material. It is the dog fur mittens you should wear in order to have your weapons to be effective and cut the bear good.
releasing animal from the forest cover
Cut twigs from a living spruce tree and set them burning on the most fresh tracks of the missing animal you can find.
building a fire to attract forest maids

Forest maids are attracted to come at nighttime campfires in remote forests of spruce and moss by lighting the fire with seven spruce twigs in there along with good pile of other firewood. Sleep on the moss by such fire and they may appear.

Quests may come in your way by talking and interacting with people.
Water is essential. Explore your surroundings until you find a source of fresh water like a lake or even a pond, then take a big gulp of fresh water and start out again
with new strength. In the winter, it won't be so easy - you'll need to use your fishing skill to make a hole in the ice. If you're wondering what's in a certain location
you can take a look and examine it if it's within your field of vision.
You can stay alive without food for weeks, but unless you have water you will die of dehydration in days.
You can zoom in and out between the large scale wilderness map and a smaller scale local terrain map. Now zoom in to a local map to explore the area you are in more closely.
The zoomed in map reflects the wilderness location accurately, so if there's a lake to the north on the wilderness map, you can find it by traveling north on the zoomed in map
as well. You may want to look in a given direction or investigate the location you are at more closely to see what's around you.
You are now on a zoomed in local terrain map. Take some time to explore your surroundings a bit. In general, long distance travel is performed on the wilderness map, and
encountering animals or people, living a settled daily life, fishing, trapping, gathering berries and such takes place on the zoomed in map.
On the zoomed in maps you can find items such as branches, fallen trees, stones etc. lying around. Depending on the season and the terrain type you may also find natural food
like mushrooms and berries. All of this is picked up the same way. Now try and pick up something you find nearby on the ground. To see what you are already carrying check out
Alright, you've picked up something. Remember that carrying heavy loads slows down your physical skill activities, makes movement slower and combat more challenging.
To survive in the wilderness, especially in the winter, you need to learn how to make a fire. That's your next task. You can find and pick up several branches and drop them
where you wish to build a fire, use your timbercraft skill to cut branches from a tree, or you can even set fire to a dry fallen tree. To place heavy trunks or a pile of firewood
to a location where you wish to build a fire you can use the push items-command. Finally, use start a fire command to light up the firewood.
Fire keeps you warm during cold weather, and will burn as long as it has enough fuel. To feed the burning fire you need to occasionally move some wood, or other burnable items,
As you probably will need to fish and hunt for your livelihood, you also need to learn to cook what you catch or kill. Now use your cookery skill to prepare some food. The most
simple recipe is just to roast raw fish or meat over the campfire. While the food is being cooked and if you don't have anything else to do, you can use the wait or rest commands
to kill some time. Your nose will tell you when the food is ready so be ready to cancel your lazy time or you will burn the food.
Raw meat and fish will spoil pretty quickly if not cooked. Recipes vary in nutrition as well as in preservation time. It's worthwhile to take some time to learn more about them at some point.
Your task is to fell a tree - for which you need to zoom in to a local map. You'll need an axe to fell bigger trees but only a knife is required for slender trunks or small trees. Now check out
your inventory, stand by the tree you wish to cut down and fell it by using your timbercraft skill. You can wield your chosen tool/weapon to get through the required equipment selection
The wood from trees in all its various forms is a very useful material which can be used for many different purposes. You can continue processing the tree you just felled with your
timbercraft skill if you like. Notice that not every felled tree is suitable for every purpose. The main difference is whether the trunk is a slender one, from a young or small tree,
or a big, fully grown one. When working with lumber, the type of axe used often has a major influence on the required working time and the quality of the result.
You can make various items by yourself; tools, weapons, clothes, even buildings. Go ahead and try to make yourself an item. You may want to check out your inventory first to see
what you have and what you need - you might want to try an easy piece of woodwork as your first attempt.
You can equip yourself pretty well with only self-made items. Sometimes, when you are unable to buy or trade for the equipment you need you will have to do with items you can
make yourself. This can actually be very rewarding and great fun if you want to live the life of a hermit or wandering adventurer.
Next you need to try out fishing, a good and relatively easy way to keep yourself fed. You can fish with a fishing rod, a spear or even a club. These are active fishing methods. You
can fish passively by using nets. Now find a suitable body of water, like a lake or river, and use your fishing skill. Before going fishing you may want to eat some food if you have
any as it's more comfortable to wait for a catch on a full stomach.
There are many factors that define how many and what kind of fish you'll catch - if you do catch anything. The fishing method and equipment used and your fishing skill do affect your
luck of course. Different types of fish are found at different depths of water and some only live in lakes and others in rivers. Your chances of catching certain fish will also depend
on the time of the day. These are things you'll learn as you gain experience with various equipment and tactics.
Sometimes it's useful to build yourself a shelter if you are planning to stay in a certain region for a long time or even just want to sleep one night more comfortably - or to stay dry
when it's raining. Therefore, your next task is to find a good place (you may want to wander around a bit to find a pleasant one) and make a shelter by using your building skill. After
your shelter is finished you may want to sleep there a night or two.
You may want to collect some firewood or food near the shelter for later use. Generally it's useful to build your shelter near water - if you don't have some with you. It also wouldn't
hurt to spend part of the evening gathering some food, fish or berries for example, for the next few days - as you now have a camp to return to when the night falls.
You should be aware that there are supernatural spirits, guardians and dwellers in The Unreal World. Your way of communicating with and affecting the spirit world are the spells and
incantations that you learn. Now review your spells and magic means profile and perform one of those, but don't select it randomly. The spells, sacrifices and incantations you perform
should always be chosen to reflect your recent deeds or the present situation.
It is adviced that you familiarize yourself with the mythology information and spell descriptions at some point. You will learn more spells during the game in
addition to the ones you start the game with.
Man is not the only being roaming The Unreal World; there are also wide variety of animals which you can't avoid encountering from time to time, and which you need to learn to hunt down
or defend yourself against. Your task now is to wander until you encounter an animal in the wilderness. You may wander around the wilderness map and try out your tracking skill here and
there. With skill, luck and patience you may be able to track down an animal, but bumping unexpectedly into wildlife while walking through the wilderness is also common. People also
sometimes share news about sightings, especially of bigger animals. If your expedition takes you far away, refer to your map of known areas to find your way in the world.
You have encountered something in the wild. If the animal encountered is not in your sight from the start, you will need to move around on the zoomed in map to find it. If you can locate
the animal (they may also escape from you very quickly) you can stalk it if you're hungry or run away if it's dangerous to you. Different animals behave in different ways, are active at
different times of the day etc., and knowing their habits is very important. If you are an inexperienced hunter, not disturbing predators that are potentially aggressive may be wise.
Now you need to hunt down and kill an animal. If the animal you have encountered is too challenging for you, back away and go track down something else, and this time make sure you are
properly prepared and equipped for the encounter. Sometimes you may need to hide and sneak (stalk) so as not to alarm a dangerous or skittish animal. Sometimes a quick rush and some running
after escaping prey is required. It's up to you whether you choose close combat or ranged weapons such as a bow and arrow to bring down the animal.
Slain animals provide meat and skin. If the animal you killed was a large one, a rare species or sacred (for example a bear) it might be justified to sacrife some of the meat
to the supernatural guardians. If you were injured during the fight you can take care of your wounds by using your physician skill.
You can use the skins of the animals you've hunted to make clothes or to trade away, especially if it's a valuable fur. However, the fresh skin needs to be tanned before it's useable
as fur or leather, and that is your next task. First use your hideworking skill to skin the carcass. After this you may want to cut up the carcass for the meat and fat. When you have
the fresh hide in your inventory, use your hideworking skill again to tan the skin; you'll need either the animal fat or some bark and some water during the process.
The tanned skin is called fur or leather depending on the skin type. Leather is useful for making clothes and other items. Fur is valuable even if not processed into a piece of clothing.
The value of the fur depends on the animal species you got it from and the season when it was obtained. In the wintertime the animals' furs are at their thickest and are much more valuable.
Skins can also be cured which preserves them until you have the time to tan them. If the fresh skin isn't cured nor tanned within a couple of days it will begin to rot and lose its value.
Rafts and punts are watercrafts used for traveling on the water. Sestas and paddles are used to pole or row them ahead. Your next task is to get yourself a watercraft of some kind and a sesta
or a paddle - then row across a lake. Notice that you can make a raft, a sesta and a paddle yourself. It's a good idea to find a lake before starting to make a raft. When you have obtained or
made a watercraft, place it on the shore, step in and wield a sesta or a paddle to move your watercraft. If you do contruct a raft further from the shore you can use move items-command to drag it
Travelling along watercourses is very convenient - keep this in mind. If you find a waterway connecting two regions important to you, you might leave a raft there for easy travel. With a sesta
you can only travel on shallow water, so you'll want to make a paddle if you plan to travel on deeper water. You can also transport loads with the watercraft by dropping the items you wish to
Even if you can survive on your own it's useful to know where you can find other people. Your next task is to find a village or settlement and enter it to see what it can offer you. There
is a vast wilderness and villages are rather rare, so you may want to equip yourself carefully for this expedition. When you are ready start roaming across the wilderness map. Settlements
usually tend to be near water and watercourses. Checking cultural regions from the map of known areas helps you to know when you are wandering in an inhabitated region. If you encounter some
wandering people you can talk to them and ask for directions to the nearest village.
Feel free to explore this settlement to see what the area and people around here can offer you. Settlements vary greatly depending on the culture of the people, from the small kota-villages of
the North to the large bustling villages of the Driik. From the larger villages you can find stores with varying goods for trade. In the small settlements of Kaumo for example you can only
trade with the people directly. All of the equipment that people carry, gather and produce - weapons, tools, food etc. are also culture-dependent.
You can trade for items with people you meet, and also trade for goods you may find from the villages. Your next task is to trade something with somebody. If you want to trade
goods from a village first pick up the the items you are interested in and then talk to somebody when you are done. To trade with individual people just talk to them. Remember that not everyone
is willing to trade with you, and they won't trade away all of their possessions.
Then there are wandering foreign traders who have expensive and rare armours and weapons they brought with them from far away. If you ever meet some foreign traders remember that they are after
furs, the higher quality the better.
At some point you may want to settle down more properly and build your own house. Your next task is to get a feeling for this. Now find a place where you would like to live for some time - feel
free to travel further from the populated areas or select a cultural territory where you feel at home - and start constructing a house of your own. It all starts by felling trees and carving
them into logs with your timbercraft skill. When you have the required materials construct a section of wall to get started.
Logs are heavy to carry, but you can easily move a pile of them by your building site using the move items-command.
Building a house is a lengthy process and the proper tools play a sigficant role in the time it takes to reach your goal. The log walls will stand waiting for you to continue the building later
on if you need to go on a hunting trip etc. for awhile. Take note that there are other contructions you can also build to make your settlement and surroundings look and work just the way you want.
In addition to hunting, fishing and gathering berries etc. agriculture is a source of independent livelihood which you need to try out now by planting something. You can spend some time looking
for a nice place for your field and then use your agriculture skill to first prepare the soil and then plant some seeds or vegetables. Remember that the ground needs to be fertilized first by
burning some wood, but you will be reminded of this when using the agriculture skill.
Seeds are hard to obtain, but preserving some of the harvested plants over the winter to be planted next spring will keep your field alive for years to come. It's a good idea to change the
location of your field after a few years to let the ground rest and grow fertile again for the future.
From many villages you can trade the items you've found or made to obtain your own animals. Animals are very useful as pack animals to carry loads and some of them can be milked. Use extended
commands to milk an animal. To pack the animal you have, use push items command to its direction. For unpacking your pack animal, use picking up items from a direction.
Having livestock also naturally secures your source of fresh meat. Your next task is to get yourself an animal, either from a village or by leashing a tame animal
you may occasionally encounter. Leash an animal by applying a rope to it. Talk to villagers for animal trading possibilities.
You may want to build a fence to keep your animals where you want. When the rope that is used as an animal leash is applied again the animal will be freed, but naturally can be leashed again
so long as it hasn't wandered off. Traveling with a big bunch animals is not a wise maneuver for a hunter since wild animals will naturally avoid such a party. Dogs can be very valuable
companions when hunting more dangerous game like bears or wolves.
For more safety while wandering in the wilderness you can ask some people to join you. Together it's a lot easier to face the setbacks and dangers of the world. Your next task is to get
yourself a companion for a short journey. Find some people and talk to them asking them to join you by selecting the "Ask for help" chat option. Besides of hiring people only to hunt
or go adventuring with you, they can help you in your daily life - for example if you need some extra hand at your building site.
Now that you have a companion feel free to carry on adventuring, hunting or whatever as you like. When you talk to your companion now, pay attention to the special command options which
can be used to give little tasks and duties to your companion.
Various traps are used in passive hunting to catch different animals. Your task now is to try this out and set a trap anywhere you like. You must zoom into the local terrain, set a trap
either with the apply command if you have a single item trap, or by using the TRAPPING skill to make one of the various trap constructions by yourself. After the trap is set zoom back out
to the wilderness map. You can freely decide the trap location and form based on what kind of animals you want to catch. If you are after carnivores, baiting the trap after it has been
set is required to make it effective at all.
Different traps are designed for different species of animals. Reading the game-info on traps is recommended.
Passive hunting using traps can be an efficient way to keep yourself warm and well-fed.
Your next task is to check the trap you have set. You usually need to wait at least for a day before it's
worthwhile to check your traps. Continue with other activities until your trap has been set for a day or
two, then find its location and zoom in to check it out.
You can locate your set traps from the map of known areas even if you've traveled far away from your hunting grounds.
If something has gotten caught into the trap you can deal with it as you please. If the trap hasn't been triggered and
you wish to set it elsewhere disassemble it first. Then you can either pick up the single item trap or the raw materials
used. If you find the trap triggered but no animal is caught in it, the animal which entered the trap may have been strong enough
to free itself from the trap. To set a triggered trap again, pick up and apply a single item trap again or use reset a trap construction option.
Your task now is to catch and kill an animal and cut the carcass for meat. You can try to catch one by using traps,
or by using your tracking skill. You can also wander around or live a settled life in the hope of a sudden encounter.
You can take some time to make more traps or other equipment, gather some food supplies for example by collecting berries
or fishing, before going hunting. You also may want to avoid encountering large carnivores at first and only follow the tracks of smaller animals.
To cook the meat you get from your prey try out your cookery skill. When dealing with a large amount of meat from a big animal it's wise to preserve
at least some of the meat using a recipe like salting, smoking or drying to make the food last longer.
You can view cultural regions from the map of known areas. Your task now is to pick up your things and travel to any area that doesn't belong to any
cultural region (appears in black color). Check out your destination first and equip yourself properly for the expedition, maybe make yourself some items or tools you might find necessary.
On your journey you may need to fill in supplies, so feel free to try out your tracking and fishing skills for example. And feel free to explore
villages or interact with people if they come in your way. When you've reached the no man's land, settle down and use your building skill to make a shelter.
There are differences in peoples' equipment and settlements depending on what culture they belong to.
The more you visit the settlements of different cultures, the more you'll find what a certain culture
can offer to you. If you walk to the very border of the known map you can choose and randomize another region to continue playing in.
You can find signs of wandering animals by using your tracking skill, and that is your next task. Tracks are easiest to find on the zoomed-in maps as they are shown graphically, but the
skill can also be used on the zoomed out wilderness map. You will probably need to search for tracks in several places to find a trail, unless an animal is encountered face to face and
a visible trail is spotted. Not all animals will leave tracks on any surface, except in the wintertime and on fresh snow. Reading the in game info about tracking is recommended, as there are
many factors involved. If it seems to take a long time to locate some tracks there's no need to rush. Keep yourself fed, take a break and continue the next day.
If you feel like it, you can try to track down the creature whose tracks you found. Use tracking again on the most recent track locations if you can't figure out the animal's direction
otherwise. If you are tracking on the wilderness scale map, an encounter will happen when you reach your prey. Although it's usually more fruitful to zoom-in to the local map if you think
you are closing in on your prey or need detailed visual information about the trail.
Now you need to catch some fish, by using any fishing technique you want. If you are lacking fishing equipment you need to go find yourself some first. Spears and clubs
can be used to catch pike from shallow waters but that's not too common - especially if you aren't a skilled fisherman. The islanders and the people of the Driik surely
possess some fishing equipment if you wish to to take this task seriously, but even a little perch from a lake nearby will be counted as a catch. So check out, make or
trade your fishing equipment, go by the water and then use your fishing skill. The map of known areas reveals the waters nearby if you have visited them already.
If you did get a big catch and do know the fisher's sacrifice for a catch-ritual, the supernatural guardians of the water may be expecting some favours in return for their generosity.
Salmon and trout are large, valuable fish that that can be caught from the rivers and especially from the rapids. Now you need to go after these desirable fish and use all of your
fishing ability to catch one. To make your fishing succesful you need to go further from the river bank, so a watercraft like a punt or a raft will be necessary.
A good salmon river may also require some exploring, the best ones are said to be found in the north.
If it seems like you are catching a lot of salmon now you may want to keep on fishing. The young salmon migrate from the rivers to the sea in the spring and and after a few years they
travel back to the rivers to reproduce - and at times like these the salmon fishing is very productive.
In the north of The Unreal World, and occasionally inland, you can find mountains. And in the mountains there are sometimes caves. Caves can provide a shelter for an adventurer during
a rainy night, but they can also be a lynx or bear den. Your next task is to find a cave and explore it to see what's inside. You can ask directions from any people you meet, but boldly
heading to northern regions will surely bring some mountains into view - but remember that not every mountain has a cave. Since the caves are dark, find or make some torches first. To
light a torch you need to apply it to a burning campfire.
Most of the caves are empty, but sometimes you can find an animal lurking inside. You can turn a cave into a relatively secure camp or a hiding place for yourself if you don't mind the
constant need of campfire or torches for a light source.
A bow can be a very efficient weapon in hunting and in combat. Your task now is to practice archery and improve your skills as a bowman. Find or make yourself a bow and practice your archery
with a live target. This can take some time but eventually, and especially after skilled shots, you will improve - as with every skill you use. You may want to spend some time making arrows
also since they do break sometimes. To shoot with a bow, have it wielded and use throw command to shoot an arrow. When you have some decent archery equipment, go bowhunting and don't expect
to see results before days, sometimes even weeks, of shooting practice.
Your archery skill has improved a bit now. Being a skilled bowman is very useful sometimes. You may want to continue experimenting with the bows to find the one that's right for you.
Crossbows are the most powerful type of bow, but they are rare and used mostly among the DriikilΣiset.
You already know some spells and incantations, and should use them to communicate with the spirit world, the supernatural guardians and the otherwordly creatures. There are spirits
that live in and take care of the forest and water, for example. You will learn more spells from other people, usually within the quests or as quest rewards. Your task now is to live
your life until you learn a spell. This requires meeting people and getting involved in quests that provide you with new magic means.
It is never a good idea to perform a spell without truly feeling an urge to do it. And it's never a good idea to constantly ask favours from the supernatural world without giving anything
in return. Use your newly gained spell wisely.
THE GREAT MAN OF THE FOREST
Your task is to go against the greatest being of the forest - the Bear. Be prepared!
You may want to get some people to help you in this task. Traps, tracking, exploring caves -
use all the ways you have learned to find and to kill the great man of the forest.
The bear has been killed. Now it's time for some rituals and sacrifices to thank the spirits. And remember to utilize the bear hide and the meat.
Njerpez warriors, foreigners from the east, have been making raids in this region. Your next task is to find their camp and kill all of them. When you find the camp you can make plans for
how and when to attack them. You'd better be prepared and properly armed too. Wandering Njerpez warriors are encountered from time to time, but in the wilderness the conflicts are easier to
avoid. In their camp you can expect to find numerous warriors so hiding and sneaking could be a very useful tactic.
Remember to take care of your wounds by using your physician skill and see if the Njerpez warriors had some useful equipment.
Trap-fences are effective especially for catching big animals that move in herds, for example wild reindeers. Your task now is to build a trap-fence of your own. Find a good place, zoom into
the terrain and start building the fence, and maybe read the hunting and fences section of the game-info browser for more information that can be useful. The shape of the fence is up to you,
but the idea here is to make a fence that an animal will start to follow and leave an opening here and there. In the openings you need to dig pits by using a shovel. When your fence is ready,
turn pits into a trap-pits and zoom back out to the wilderness map to finish the task. The fence needs to be rather long to be effective.
Your trap fence is now finished and you can leave it to hopefully catch something. You can also use regular traps instead of pits and also bait your traps to attract carnivores. Trap-fences
are a long-term passive hunting construction. Just remember to reset the traps that got triggered during use and set fresh baits (if you are after carnivores) whenever you check your traplines.
Your clothes wear out as time goes by so you'll need to get or make new clothes eventually. You can make some clothes by yourself and that's your next task: to make yourself some fur clothing.
A hunter wearing a wolf or bear fur cloak for example is an impressive sight, but any fur and piece of clothing will do for now. To get fur you first need to find and kill a fur-bearing animal
(a fox, hare, glutton, or bear for example) and then use your hideworking skill to skin the animal and to tan the skin. After the skin is tanned you can make clothing out of it. Naturally the
bigger the cloth the more fur you will need, but smaller pieces of fur can be used to complete an item if you have enough of them to put together.
In addition to providing material for clothing, some furs are very valuable in trading. You can also make clothes out of leather, but the fur provides more protection and warmth.
First of all you must now secure your source of livelihood and gather yourself something to eat for the next few days. Check out your inventory to see what you already carry and fill your
supplies the way you want: use your fishing skill, or tracking skill to track down and hunt animals, or if it's a suitable time of the year zoom into the terrain to gather berries or mushrooms.
Or trade food from the people you meet if that's what suits you best. When you think you have enough food for at least five days eat something - and if you have plenty of food, the task is
completed and you are ready to move on.
When one hunts down a big elk or other large animal, there's no need to worry about food for weeks. But sometimes even if you feel your supplies are sufficient some extra won't hurt -
especially if there's a longer expedition planned up ahead. Then again a very skilled hunter or fisherman can wander around carrying barely more than a bow or a fishing rod and catch himself a
The northern people are well known for their unique supernatural powers and sorcery. It is commonly held that they can drive supernatural powers into the weapons they make, especially knives
and bows. And with no doubt northern knives and bows are strong and effective weapons, with or without the use of sorcery. Your next task is to obtain a northern bow or a northern knife. Travel
to the northern reaches of the world, and find someone willing to trade you one of these items. Then, get a feeling for your new and unique piece of northern weaponry by wielding it.
If you master the oath of iron ritual you can drive supernatural powers into your metal weapons by yourself. To get a better feel for your new weapon you can try to use it the next time
Salt is rare, valuable, and very useful. Salt production generally takes place on an archipelago. Driik and the regions of the Islanders are the main areas where you can obtain salt.
Salt is rarely found inland, but may be brought in by foreign traders and tradesmen of the inland. Your task is to travel to an archipelago of The Unreal World to find and trade for
some bags of salt. Remember that you need to get the salt
by trading, and only by trading. Be sure to bring something along that you can trade for the salt.
If you haven't tried salting meat or fish before, now would be a good time. The hardship of obtaining salt is compensated when you can make yourself a decent supply of salted meat or fish.
Your next task is to build yourself a house - a complete house. So don't rush! Find a territory and terrain which suits you. You want a place that you can call home for some time.
You can also build yourself a hunting cottage somewhere. The shape and size of the house is up you, as is its usage. The task isn't complete until your house has all the walls up
and you've started working on ceiling and floor. Be sure to equip yourself with the proper axes - like having a carving axe and broad axe for making logs and log walls properly.
Move items-command is very useful when working with heavy lumber and organizing your piles of raw material like boards etc.
Your house is coming along nicely. If this is to be your home, you may also want to build a storehouse or a cellar nearby. Perhaps in the future you might have some animals in a fenced
pen, or in a little field nearby.
The sauna is a place for cleaning up, but also for physical and mental relaxation, healing, and giving birth. Your task now is to find a sauna, which exist in nearly every settled
village - and sometimes even in vagabond settlements. You will recognize the sauna as being a small building with a fireplace alike sauna stove, and a tub of water. Heat up the sauna
for several hours by building a fire in the sauna stove. Then take off your clothes, pick up the tub of water and apply it beside the sauna stove to throw water on top of it for steam.
Loading firewood into the sauna stove before making a fire is easiest by having a pile of firewood beside your feet and using push items-commands.
If you are feeling ill, exhausted, or even wounded, taking a sauna bath can be a source of relief for your ailments.
Taking a sauna bath can also be a spiritual experience. There are supernatural beings taking care of and living in the sauna,
so enjoy your bath with a grateful attitude.
Elk are the biggest animals in The Unreal World, and thus the most wanted prey when one is after a large amount of meat at once. Your next task is to hunt down an elk,
but it must also be a big one. When you encounter an animal you can look at it to see if it's a small or a big individual - or an average one if no size is
indicated in the description. But now you are after big game. After finding and bringing the animal down, cut it for meat and the task will be completed. Of course you may skin it first by using
your hideworking skill. Use any hunting techniques you have mastered or find useful to find and catch your elk. You should expect to encounter several elks before finding a large one.
The amount of meat, and also the size of the skin you get from the slain animals is dependent of the animal size. In case of smaller animals the difference isn't that much, but when it comes
to elks for example you may get tens of pounds more meat from a big individual than what you would get from a smaller one.
Swamps and bogs are a strange and intimidating terrain feature. There are stories about rare occasions when both people and animals have been sacrificed and buried into peat bogs. Weapons and
other items are sometimes hidden or sacrificially buried into bogs. Your task now is to sacrificially bury some sort of metal weapon. A knife, a sword or an axe. Bogs are also a source of ore
which is used to make iron, and thus the very origin of the iron. Go to the swamp or bog at night, build a fire, and then throw the weapon into the waters of the open bog. This is a gesture of
respect for the bog and a way to ritually bond yourself with the iron more closely.
When there's need for you to sacrifice meat for the supernatural guardians, coming to butcher an animal at the swamp is the way to do it with utmost dedication.
Certain bog types are also a source of tasty berries in the autumn.

Furs from the Kaumo region are of very high quality and hunters from far away places regularly go to Kaumo to hunt for beavers, squirrels, and foxes. Your task now is to travel to Kaumo to hunt
for some high quality fur. When you are at Kaumo your task is to
hunt for a valued fur bearing animal and use your hideworking skill to skin it. The animal can be for example a fox, a lynx, a beaver, and so on. Feel free to use any hunting technique you like.
Trying to use a fox-trap could be good choice here. And remember: you need to hunt, kill and skin the animal in the Kaumo region.
Feel free to continue your hunt for the fur now that you are at the esteemed hunting grounds. If you ever encounter foreign traders, carrying valuable furs with you may provide you with something
to trade for metal armours and swords. Even if furs from squirrels, polecats and other small animals aren't big enough for making clothes easily, there's a reason to keep hunting them. Especially
if you find yourself in an area that has lots of them.
Traders from far away countries come to the north, to The Unreal World, after furs. They are willing to trade their metal armours and weapons for these high quality furs. Foreign traders are now
in this region. Your task is to find them and to trade with them. If you aren't carrying any furs with, trying to trade with them will be rather fruitless. If this is the case you must first
get yourself some furs. Then wander around, or you can also try to find their tracks, until you find them and then make a succesful trade with some of them.

The wilderness carries berries and mushrooms from early spring to late winter, and people grow crops on their fields. Your task now is to harvest some of the gifts the earth produces,
either from a field of your own, or someone elses - or to pick berries or mushrooms. If the season is now winter in its darkest and coldest phase, you need to wait for spring. If it's autumn,
it should be easy to find something to harvest. To harvest a plant you need to just simply pick it up. The herblore skill can be used to recognize unknown plants and identify their properties.
The type of berries or mushrooms found in the wilderness depends on the terrain type and the season. You can find mushrooms suprisingly late in the autumn, even after the first snow has come.
With mushrooms some caution may be required, since some of them are very poisonous.
Now you need to travel over the water. Find an island and make your way to it by travelling on the wilderness map. This way you'll spot any nearby islands from a good distance away. There are
some big lakes in the inland, and but an island may not be easy to find. If you are at the archipelago or near the sea, there are lots of bigger and smaller islands. In this task we're after
a small, cosy island. You of course need to get or make yourself a watercraft also, and a paddle. A punt is a convenient watercraft since it can be carried with you. If you're going to make a
raft, it's best to wait until you've already spotted an island to do so. Rafts are heavy, and having to move it to another lake if you don't find an island here may prove to be a difficult task.
Now that you are on an island, and if it's not too big, it's possible to spend your time there securely and without being disturbed. Islands are also good places to hide some of your most precious
goods. If you have animals, herding them onto an island will help protect them from wolves and other predators.
There are four different times of the year. The seasons are spring, summer, autumn and the winter. Seasons have a great influence on daily life. The winters are cold and dark, and the lakes get
covered with thick ice - a decent food supply collected in the autumn will help you to survive in the colder months. In the spring nature wakes up and begins a new life as vegetation starts to
grow, mostly peaking in the late summer and then dying off in the late autumn. Your task now is to experience a little of this change of the seasons and survive until next month. You won't see a
large seasonal change in a single month, but each and every day means the next season is just a bit closer. Spend your days as you please.
It can be of great use to follow the marks of nature while living your life in The Unreal World, especially knowing what season certain berries or mushrooms grow in, and so on. Hunting and
fishing are regularly practiced throughout the year, but the shorter, frozen days of winter make these activities more difficult.
Your task now is to please the spirits of the forest by some spell or a sacrifice. Notice that the spell must be performed according to a deed you have done - otherwise it may be
meaningless. If you have just recently done something that you feel is worthy of a certain spell or a sacrifice, perform it now. Otherwise wait for an opportunity to please the spirits of the forest.
The forest has been pleased, and your travels will feel just a bit safer and more secure now.
